basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 30.' and it opens 'Vers. 30. Egresso Jacob venit Esau. Quod vero Esau ad patrem revertitur, populi prioris'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 30. Egresso Jacob venit Esau. Quod vero Esau ad patrem revertitur, populi prioris in fine saeculi conversionem designat, de qua Psalmista dixerat: Convertentur ad vesperam, et famem patientur ut canes (Psal. LVIII, 15). Et propheta: Aperuerunt ora sua, sicut pauper comedens in abscondito.
